Regarding interventions (Q6/Q7), the distinction in selectivity based on intervention type was essential but intuitive: generic emails allow for higher false positives, whereas personalized advisor contact demands precision to avoid unnecessary anxiety or wasted time. I agree with S1 and A1 that without high explainability (Q4), using Absalon data or sensitive markers like disability status creates a surveillance trap rather than support.
